title: Lamb Tagine
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb shoulder with warm spices
excerpt: Lamb shoulder braised for two hours with cinnamon, cumin, allspice and ginger until it collapses into a richly spiced sauce. Traditional recipes add dried apricots for sweetness; since they are not in the ingredient table here, a tablespoon of honey does the same work. Scatter with toasted flaked almonds before serving for a textural contrast.
sourceNotes: Lamb tagine is central to Moroccan celebratory cooking; the combination of warm spices and sweet additions like dried fruit traces back to medieval Arab culinary manuscripts that influenced North African kitchens.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, then freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of stock.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the day after cooking. Refrigerate overnight and reheat slowly over a low heat, adding a splash of water if needed.

content.text: Traditional Moroccan lamb tagine often includes dried apricots, which provide a floral sweetness that balances the warm spices. This recipe uses a tablespoon of honey in their place, which gives a similar sweetness without the specific flavour of apricot. If you can source dried apricots, add 80g of the unsulphured variety along with the tomatoes. The honey here compensates for their absence, but the dish is still very good without them. Toasted flaked almonds scattered over at the end provide a crunch that the slow braise lacks.

items.prepNote: to provide sweetness in place of the traditional dried apricots
toasted in a dry pan until golden, to scatter over before serving

content.text: Heat a drizzle of oil in a large, heavy-based pot over a high heat. Season the lamb pieces and brown in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply coloured all over. Do not crowd the pan. Remove each batch to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the pot with a pinch of salt and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, fresh ginger, cinnamon, cumin, coriander and allspice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the spices smell fragrant.

Add the tinned tomatoes, honey and stock. Stir to combine. Return the browned lamb to the pot, pushing the pieces into the liquid. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on a low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes, stirring once halfway through.
Remove the lid and cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the lamb is very tender, falling apart at the edges. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve over couscous, scattered with fresh coriander and toasted flaked almonds. The almonds add crunch and a nutty richness that the slow braise needs.

items.symptom: Lamb is still tough after 1.5 hours
items.cause: Shoulder cut varies and some pieces take longer; the braise temperature may be too low
items.fix: Continue cooking with the lid on at a steady simmer for another 30 minutes. Lamb shoulder should shred easily when pressed with a fork when done.

items.cause: Too much honey or the tinned tomatoes were very sweet
items.fix: Add a splash of lemon juice or a small pinch of salt to bring the flavour back into balance.
